To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the challenges faced by isolated learners are significant, and that the one size fits approach to online learning is inadequate.
the online learning environment is not suitable for all students.
the challenges faced by students in online learning are the same as those in any learning environment, but they are exacerbated by the lack of face-to-face contact.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the experiences of students and academic staff when learning and teaching is conducted online, with a particular focus on the challenges faced by students who are isolated from the university community.
understanding how to support the isolated learner and how to better engage this learner in the online environment.
the experiences of external students who engage with the university online.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
online delivery can be a very effective way of engaging students in learning, particularly when the online environment is designed and developed with the needs of the students in mind.
the challenges of online learning are significant and the isolation experienced by many external students can be exacerbated by the lack of support and engagement provided by their lecturers.
online delivery of units of study is not a panacea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are all learners and teachers and that the more we can learn together the better we will be at supporting and engaging students in online learning environments.
the challenges faced by the external student can be overcome by the provision of a range of support mechanisms and a flexible and responsive teaching approach.
the online environment provides an opportunity to engage with students who may not otherwise have access to university education and to provide a flexible and accessible mode of study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online delivery of units is a complex and demanding process.

we should not assume that the same learning activities will have the same effect in different learning modes, or that the same learning outcomes will be achieved in the same way across all delivery modes.
we need to be mindful of the needs of the external students and provide them with a sense of belonging and connectedness to the institution and their peers.
